title: What If You Jumped From the Edge of Space?

scenes.text: What if you jumped from the edge of space? One man did, and beat the speed of sound.
In 2012, Felix Baumgartner jumped from a balloon about thirty-nine kilometers up, far higher than airliners fly.
The air up there is so thin that he sped up fast. He hit about thirteen hundred kilometers an hour, Mach 1.25, with no engine.
Within the first minute he began to spin out of control, a spin that could have been fatal.
He steadied himself, and fell for four minutes nineteen seconds before his parachute opened.
He landed safely in the New Mexico desert, the first human to break the sound barrier with only his body.
